content:
A data lakehouse is a modern data architecture that combines the best features of data lakes and data warehouses. Let me break down the key characteristics and differences:

Data Warehouse:
- Structured data only
- Predefined schema (schema-on-write)
- Optimized for complex queries
- Expensive storage
- Limited scalability
- Best for processed, analytical data
- Typically uses relational databases
- Higher performance for structured queries
- Expensive to maintain

Data Lake:
- Stores raw, unstructured data
- Schema-on-read
- Highly scalable
- Very cost-effective storage
- Can handle multiple data types
- Stores raw data in native format
- Less expensive
- More flexible

Data Lakehouse:
- Combines benefits of both
- Supports structured and unstructured data
- Provides ACID transactions
- Uses open file formats (Parquet, Delta)
- Supports machine learning and analytics
- More flexible schema
- Lower cost storage
- Better performance
- Supports direct querying of raw data
- Uses technologies like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg

Key Technologies:
- Databricks Delta Lake
- Apache Iceberg
- Amazon Athena
- Google BigQuery
- Snowflake

Main advantages:
- Unified data platform
- Reduced data movement
- Lower total cost of ownership
- More flexible data management
